CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics
Accreditation: CAP #[redacted ID], CLIA #[redacted ID]

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: Not applicable (prenatal)
Medical Record #: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 35 years
Gestational Age: 16 weeks
Indication for Testing: Advanced maternal age, screening for chromosomal abnormalities including trisomy 21
Previous Testing: Rapid PCR analysis performed (see note below)

TEST PERFORMED
Conventional Cytogenetic Analysis - G-banded Karyotype

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured according to standard protocols. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells were analyzed at the 400-550 band level of resolution. Two independent cultures were established to minimize the risk of maternal cell contamination and culture artifacts.

RESULTS
Karyotype: 46,XY

INTERPRETATION
This analysis reveals a normal male chromosome complement with 46 chromosomes including XY sex chromosomes. No numerical or structural chromosomal abnormalities were detected. Specifically, there is no evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), or sex chromosome aneuploidies.

The normal male karyotype indicates low risk for chromosomal disorders detectable by conventional cytogenetic analysis.

LIMITATIONS
This test detects chromosomal abnormalities at the resolution of G-banded analysis (approximately 5-10 Mb). Smaller deletions, duplications, or balanced rearrangements below this resolution may not be detected. This analysis does not detect single gene disorders, methylation abnormalities, or low-level mosaicism (<10%).

NOTE
This report supersedes the previous rapid PCR analysis report. The karyotype analysis provides comprehensive chromosomal evaluation beyond the targeted aneuploidies assessed by rapid PCR.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results in the context of the pregnancy
2. Routine prenatal care should continue as indicated
3. No additional cytogenetic testing is indicated based on these results

This analysis was performed and interpreted according to ACMG standards and guidelines for constitutional cytogenomic microarray analysis.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Clinical Cytogenetics
